metadata.case_name: WONG KI v. WONG TUNG SING AND OTHERS

injuries.description: Ruptured left eyeball with corneo-scleral laceration; penetrating injury to the iris and crystalline lens of left eye; aphakic left eye with inferior corneal scar; chronic rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (inferior) and prior infero-temporal retinal tear.
source: · Ruptured left eyeball with corneo-scleral laceration;
· Penetrating injury to the iris and crystalline lens of left eye.
When Mr Wong attended our joint ophthalmic assessment on 26th February 2008, an asymptomatic inferior chronic rhegmatogenous retinal detachment was found in his left eye.
On 14th March 2008, Mr Wong was admitted to the DOVS of PWH for operation to repair the retinal detachment under general anaesthesia.

Upon another examination on 14 August 2009, the visual acuity was 20/10 for his right eye and 2/200 for his left eye. The right eye was unremarkable but the left eye was aphakic (without the lens) and with inferior corneal scar.
injuries.icd_description: Ocular laceration or rupture with prolapse or loss of intraocular tissue, unilateral

injuries.description: Post-traumatic Stress Disorder with an element of Depression (psychiatric condition) following the industrial accident.
source: “He first attended West Kowloon Psychiatric Centre on 29 September 2008. He had injury of his left eye during an industrial accident in 2005. After that accident, he developed depressive mood, loss of interest, negative thoughts, easy irritability, flashbacks of that accident, poor sleep and appetite, vague suicidal idea and worries about his future. He had no abnormal perception or belief. He stayed at home most of the time. His diagnosis was Post-traumatic Stress Disorder with an element of Depression."

manifestations.description: Sharp pain in the left eye immediately after glass granule entered the eye.
Immediate loss of vision in left eye; initial left eye visual acuity recorded as CF (Counting Fingers).

Best corrected visual acuity of the left eye was 20/200 (4 March 2009) and 2/200 (14 August 2009); experts opined 100% visual impairment in left eye (limited to hand movement) equivalent to 20% impairment of the whole person.
Inferior corneal scar in left eye.
Perception of distance and 3-dimensional perception affected; constricted field of vision; fine visual discrimination affected.

Relatively minor psychiatric symptoms: depressive mood, loss of interest, negative thoughts, easy irritability, flashbacks, poor sleep and appetite, vague suicidal idea, worries about future; stayed at home most of the time.

treatments_received: Primary repair of the corneo-scleral laceration
Operation to repair retinal detachment (14 March 2008)
treatments_future: Implantation of intraocular lens and pupilloplasty (planned; aborted on 27 August 2009)

losses.description: 100% visual impairment in his left eye (limited to hand movement) equivalent to 20% impairment of the whole person; reduced distance and 3-dimensional perception, constricted visual field and impaired fine visual discrimination.

Experts stated it is not suitable for Mr Wong to resume his previous job in construction sites or to take up jobs that require operation of dangerous machines; types of suitable jobs listed are limited.
After the accident he developed PTSD with depressive symptoms and "stayed at home most of the time."

comparable_cases.case_name: Ho Yam Pan v Tse Tak Ming trading as Ken’s Company
comparable_cases.injury_description: Construction site worker. Cutting blade broke and hurt right eye. Despite surgery, right eye lost light perception; assessed 100% permanent disability of that eye, equivalent to 25% impairment of the visual system or 24% impairment of the whole person.

comparable_cases.case_name: Chan Kwok Ping v Hop Yick Engineering Company (a firm) & Another
comparable_cases.injury_description: Painter. Right eye hit by corrosive alkaline whitewash causing large corneal ulcer and vascularised corneal scar; visual acuity reduced to 3/60; visual disability assessed at 90% in the right eye.

comparable_cases.case_name: Lai Ka Wai v Lo Tak Cheung trading as Luen Fat Construction Company & Others
comparable_cases.injury_description: Construction site worker. Blinded in left eye completely after spectacles broken; assessed 24% permanent disability of visual system.

comparable_cases.case_name: Sze Ping Chui v Lau Ching Wai
comparable_cases.injury_description: Plasterer. Left eye ruptured by tile fragments with 5mm full thickness corneal laceration at visual axis and damaged lens; visual acuity assessed at 35%, permanent disability 67% or 16% impairment of the whole person.
